paper.title: Scalable Circuit Learning for Interpreting Large Language Models

read: full text (arXiv HTML): Sections 1-5, Limitations and Appendices B (assumptions), C (optimisation, per-case results, SAE procedure, domain generalisation), D (sparsity ablation, coefficient statistics, faithfulness, Bias-in-Bios); A (proofs) skimmed

claims.claim: The connections between components of a transformer that make up a circuit for a task can be recovered from activations alone, with no activation patching or backward passes, by fitting an L1-penalised linear regression of each layer's components on those of earlier layers (respecting the model's computation order), about as accurately as gradient-based attribution-patching methods but at a fraction of their cost. Supported only if, on the 16 main synthetic transformers with known circuits in InterpBench plus the real indirect-object-identification case, the regression's mean structural Hamming distance to the true circuit is within 0.25 of edge attribution patching with integrated gradients and below plain edge attribution patching, it differs from the integrated-gradients method by at most 1 on every synthetic case, and its mean runtime is at most half that method's and below plain attribution patching's.
claims.decision_rule: Mean SHD over 17 tasks <= EAP-ig + 0.25 and < EAP; per-case |SHD - EAP-ig| <= 1 on all 16 cases; runtime <= 0.5x EAP-ig and < EAP.

claims.claim: A sparse linear predictor fitted on a language model's sparse-autoencoder features is enough to find the spurious features to remove when debiasing a classifier, so the costly intervention-based search for causally relevant features is unnecessary for this use. Supported only if, on Bias-in-Bios (predict profession from biographies, training set where gender and profession are correlated, balanced test set) for Pythia-70M, Gemma-2-2B and Gemma-2-9B, zeroing the gender features it ranks highest gives profession accuracy at least that of the intervention-based feature-ablation method in every model, both with and without retraining the classifier afterwards; with retraining, also above concept-bottleneck and sparse linear probing in every model; gender stays predictable at no more than 53% (chance 50%); and the feature search takes at most a fifth of the intervention method's runtime in every model.
claims.decision_rule: Prof. acc >= SHIFT (and retrain >= SHIFT-retrain) on all 3 models; retrain > cbp and linear probing on all 3; gender <= 53%; runtime <= 0.2x SHIFT on all 3.

experiments.text: Define the regression surrogate. Setup: collect activations of the chosen components (neurons, attention or MLP outputs, or SAE features), averaged over tokens, for each prompt; for neurons, clean and corrupted prompts are pooled into one observational dataset; fit X = A^T X with an L1 penalty, the adjacency A forced block upper triangular so that later layers cannot feed earlier ones (acyclicity from the computation order), solved as multi-output Lasso problems with FISTA and backtracking on one A100. For SAE features (dimension D), regress each layer's features on the previous layer's, and fit a sparse predictor from one layer's features to the task label; edges are the non-zero coefficients. The model is presented as a linear surrogate for the dependency skeleton, not exact causal effects; a nonlinear variant is also given.

Compare structural accuracy and cost on a benchmark with known circuits. Setup: InterpBench, 16 main semi-synthetic transformer cases plus the real IOI case, against edge attribution patching (EAP) and EAP with integrated gradients (EAP-ig) on the same prompts; structural Hamming distance to the ground-truth circuit and wall-clock runtime, three trials on one A100. Result: mean SHD 3.16 for the linear regression against 2.98 for EAP-ig and 3.61 for EAP; mean runtime 16.3 s against 49.1 s and 33.7 s. Per case, it equals EAP-ig in mean and standard deviation on 11 of 16 cases and differs by at most 1 on the rest (cases 4, 19, 29, 35 slightly worse); run-to-run standard deviation is 0 for all methods on 11 cases.

Break the errors down. Setup: per-case false positives and false negatives on the 16 synthetic cases. Result: missed edges dominate for all methods (about 81% of the regression's errors, 75% for EAP-ig, 72% for EAP); the regression adds the fewest spurious edges (0.44 per case against 0.54 and 0.85) but misses slightly more (1.90 against 1.65 for EAP-ig), losing edges EAP-ig finds on cases 19, 29 and 35; overall precision / recall 0.705 / 0.398 against 0.852 / 0.491 for EAP-ig and 0.514 / 0.299 for EAP. All methods fail on cases 13 and 21.

Check whether the linear form loses accuracy. Setup: a nonlinear variant of the same regression on InterpBench. Result: mean SHD 2.84, marginally better than the linear version, at 3.7 times its runtime, slower than EAP-ig in most cases.

Scale to sparse-autoencoder features of a real model. Setup: GPT-2 small with OpenAI's 32,768-feature SAEs on block outputs of all 12 layers, 8,551 CoLA training sentences; learn adjacencies between consecutive layers and a sparse predictor of grammatical acceptability; label features by top-activating tokens across prompts and by single-token perturbations; evaluate faithfulness and completeness of the learned circuit with feature (node) ablation against the intervention-based SHIFT circuit, and with edge ablation, which SHIFT cannot do. Result: traced paths show concepts persisting across layers ('-self' from layer 8 to 12), merging and dropping, and some apparently anti-causal or spurious links ('-self' linked to 'hunger/thirst'); node-ablation faithfulness and completeness are comparable to SHIFT (reported only in a figure), and a small set of edges governs the prediction. The case study is qualitative and limited to GPT-2 small.

Check sensitivity to the sparsity penalty. Setup: on the CoLA final-layer predictor, vary lambda from 0 to 5e-4. Result: lambda = 0 overfits (99.36% train, 71.10% test accuracy); lambda = 1e-5 gives the best test accuracy (72.77%); larger values lower both (70.28% at 5e-4); at the chosen value 82.2% of coefficients are below 0.01 and the top 5 features dominate.

Set up the debiasing task. Setup: Bias-in-Bios profession classification with a training set in which gender and profession are correlated and a balanced test set; Pythia-70M (SAEs of Marks et al.) and Gemma-2-2B and 9B (Gemma Scope SAEs), features from one layer averaged over tokens; fit a sparse linear classifier on them, rank by coefficient magnitude, have a person identify gender-related features among the top ones, zero them and evaluate with the original classifier or a retrained one. Baselines: classifier on the biased set, concept-bottleneck probing, k-sparse linear probing on the same features, SHIFT (patching-based feature selection with manual ablation, with and without retraining); a classifier trained on the balanced set as an upper bound. Metrics: profession accuracy, gender predictability (50% ideal) and worst-group accuracy.

Compare accuracy and cost. Result: profession accuracy without retraining 90.5 / 77.5 / 81.5% (Pythia-70M / Gemma-2-2B / 9B) against 88.5 / 72.8 / 77.1% for SHIFT; with retraining 94.2 / 95.1 / 96.9% against 93.1 / 94.2 / 96.0% for SHIFT-retrain, 84.0 / 90.5 / 95.0% for linear probing and 83.3 / 90.1 / 94.7% for concept-bottleneck probing (balanced-set oracle 93.0 / 95.1 / 95.7%). Gender predictability 50.1 / 50.7 / 50.3% without and 50.6 / 52.8 / 50.5% with retraining; worst-group accuracy 88.7 / 92.9 / 91.5% with retraining. Runtime 36.5 / 47.2 / 107.4 s against 257.6 / 371.2 / 908.4 s for SHIFT, with 41 / 55 / 59 features selected against 49 / 65 / 71.

Note what the runtime and accuracy comparisons leave out. Setup: runtimes exclude the manual step of judging which top-ranked features are gender-related, which both methods require; the predictor is in effect a sparse linear classifier on the same features, and plain linear probing without any ablation already reaches 90.5% and 95.0% on the Gemma models, so the non-retrained variant's lower Gemma accuracy (77.5%, 81.5%) means most of the retrained gain comes from refitting the classifier. The authors attribute the small accuracy margins to operating on disentangled SAE features rather than to circuit learning.

dropped: Complexity propositions (cost bounds versus EAP-ig, proofs only); second traced circuit example.
notes: Drafted from scratch from arXiv HTML for the dataset50 rebuild, without consulting earlier claims or references. c0: 3.16 vs 2.98 = +0.18; runtime 16.3/49.1 = 0.33. c1 runtime ratios 0.14 / 0.13 / 0.12; gender max 52.8 (retrain, Gemma-2-2B). Faithfulness results exist only as a figure, so no numeric bar is set on them.
